title.en: Reflection of light and spherical mirrors

text.en: In a plane mirror you see yourself the same size, and left appears right. A curved spoon, though, shows you upside-down and smaller. Mirrors follow clear laws.

Laws of reflection: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, and the incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in the same plane.
A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect image the same size as the object, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.
A concave mirror curves inwards and converges light; a convex mirror curves outwards and diverges light.
The focal length f of a spherical mirror is half its radius of curvature R, f = R/2.
Mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, and magnification m = - v/u.
A concave mirror is used in shaving mirrors, torches and headlights; a convex mirror in vehicles as a rear-view mirror because it gives a wider field of view.
Rough surfaces scatter light in many directions (diffuse reflection).

problem.en: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature 20 cm. Find its focal length.

why.en: The principal focus lies 10 cm from the mirror.

prompt.en: State the two laws of reflection and name the mirror used in vehicles.

requiredIdeas.en: Rays and normal in one plane

commonMisconceptions.en: Measuring angles from the mirror instead of the normal

points.en: Angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
Plane mirror: virtual, erect, same size.
Convex mirrors give a wider view.
